executive_summary: The whitepaper outlines an innovative decentralized consensus architecture. While cryptographic principles are sound, key operational risks stem from majority hashrate concentration vulnerabilities and confirmation depth latency before finality.

top_risks.description: 51% mining power majority can theoretically rewrite recent block history and double-spend.
Settlement latency requires multiple confirmation blocks before economic finality is guaranteed.
Long-term security budget transitions from block subsidies to transaction fees with unknown fee market stability.

all_findings.description: Consensus vulnerability identified in section 1: hash power concentration risk.
all_findings.evidence_quote: Any attacker controlling majority computing power can outpace honest nodes.

all_findings.description: Confirmation latency and chain reorganization risk prior to settlement finality.
all_findings.evidence_quote: Nodes accept the longest proof-of-work chain as authoritative truth.
